El jue, 18 ene 2024 a las 11:58, hongyi sun (<shy9...@gmail.com>) escribió:
Dear All,

i am conducting a study by running CFA model. For my variables, which contains the dummy variables and the continuous variables, In this case ,
1) If i turn all the continuous variables to dummy variables, should i use "ordered = TRUE" ?

Not sure why you would want to do that, it doesn't seem like a good idea. Also, how are you planning to do it, by applying a threshold? In any case, I understand that the answer to your question is "yes, you should use `ordered = TRUE`" if all your observable variables are turned into categorical.
2) if i keep using mix variables, how to make lavvan Identify whether this variable is actually dummy variables or continoous variables.

From the `lavaan` help page:

ordered

Character vector. Only used if the data is in a data.frame. Treat these variables as ordered (ordinal) variables, if they are endogenous in the model. Importantly, all other variables will be treated as numeric (unless they are declared as ordered in the data.frame.) Since 0.6-4, ordered can also be logical. If TRUE, all observed endogenous variables are treated as ordered (ordinal). If FALSE, all observed endogenous variables are considered to be numeric (again, unless they are declared as ordered in the data.frame.)


That is, you have several options:
  • Make sure your "dummy" variables are of type `ordered` your data.frame.
  • Declare the "dummy" ones as ordered by variable name, using a character vector, in the `ordered` argument to lavaan.
  • Declare the "dummy" ones as ordered by position using a logical vector, in the `ordered` argument to lavaan (where a `TRUE` value means that a variable in that position is to be treated as ordinal, and `FALSE` that it is to be treated as numerical).
3) my sample size is more than 5000, which estimator is suitable for this kind of mix variables model.
I understand your sample size is big enough to not be a limiting factor. You should consider other criteria to decide the best estimator.

messages.subject: Re: how toHow to address the multiple types of variables in one CFA model
parts:
Let's say your data.frame contains the following variables: `probe_1`, `probe_2`, `diagnostic_1`, `diagnostic_2`. Let's assume `probe_1` and `probe_2` are quantitative variables, and `diagnostic_1` and `diagnostic_2` are dichotomous variables with values " 1=with such disease, 0=without such disease". Then, in your call to `lavaan()` or `cfa()`, you can add the argument:

`ordered = c("diagnostic_1", "diagnostic_1")`

This of course assuming all the variables in your data frame are numeric (including the first two ones). If you don't know what I mean by "numeric variables", you probably need to get a better understanding of the basics of data types in R. I suggest a Google search with precisely the terms data types in R "data types R".

Hope this helps!

--
